grokowski.keyNumberSensitivity: Bills -7 is meaningfully better than -7.5 because a 7-point Buffalo win pushes instead of losing. At -6.5 that same 7-point win becomes a cover, which is a real upgrade; I would like the favorite more there and would back off if forced to lay -7.5.
grokowski.analysisMarkdown:
I like Bills -7 here, as a lean I would take but not press. I have Buffalo a little bigger than seven at home, so laying this number with a push if they win by a touchdown is the side I want. Three games of form are still messy, so this is not an automatic play.

The market is Bills -7 at -105 and Patriots +7 at -115. Most books are at seven, a few at six and a half, and the total is 48.5, which is higher than I want. Seven is material: a Bills win by exactly a touchdown pushes at this number, covers at -6.5, and loses at -7.5. I would rather sit here than lay the extra half.

New England has scored 12 points a game through three weeks, including a 6-point loss at Jacksonville, after a much stronger offensive season a year ago. That collapse is why Buffalo is a real home favorite in a division game. Buffalo is unbeaten and should still land in the high 20s even after a quieter 24-point win over the Chargers, against a Patriots defense that has been respectable, not dominant. Buffalo's defense has allowed 26 a game, so if New England is merely mediocre, some Patriots points stay on the board.

What keeps me from calling it a bet is New England's offense snapping back toward last year. Buffalo has already been giving up points, and a one-score AFC East game would leave Bills -7 as a push or a loss.

**Bills -7: ~53% cover probability**
**Patriots +7: ~40%**
**Fair-ish score: Patriots 18, Bills 27**
**Projected total: ~45**

So at the exact line I would choose Bills -7. You're laying -105, which only needs a little over 51 percent, and I have the cover rate only in the low 50s, so I would not press it. If it moved to -7.5, I would be noticeably less interested because a touchdown win becomes a loss instead of a push.

keyDrivers.summary: New England has scored 12 points per game with clearly negative offensive EPA through three games, including a 6-point outing at Jacksonville, after putting up 28.8 per game last season. That collapse is the main reason Buffalo is a solid home favorite and why the total is not a shootout.

Buffalo is 3-0 and scoring 33.7 points per game with strongly positive offensive EPA and 6.8 yards per play. Even after a quieter 24-point win over the Chargers, that unit should still land in the high 20s against a Patriots defense that has been respectable but not dominant.

Buffalo's defense has allowed 26 points per game and positive EPA per play, so this is not a shutdown spot. If New England's offense is even mediocre rather than broken, some Patriots points stay on the board and the total does not crash into the low 40s.

Last season both teams were efficient, high-scoring clubs with nearly identical offensive EPA, and three unadjusted games are a noisy sample with ugly turnover rates. The current 21-point scoring gap should be regressed, which trims Buffalo's number off a blowout and keeps the projected total near the mid-40s.

grokowski.mainRisk: New England's offense is closer to last season's 28.8 points per game than to this year's 12, turning a Buffalo control game into a one-score AFC East matchup.
